page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.12xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and custom ARMv9-based AWS Graviton processors. It features 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The memory configuration includes 192.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. The CPU cache architecture consists of 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, but it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in memory operations and multi-threaded processing. The server achieved top 10% rankings in large-block memory bandwidth with 435.26 GB/sec read and 217.09 GB/sec write speeds, PassMark memory score, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 522.44 GB/sec. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 24004.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 81856.98. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench text processing scoring in the average range.

Tradeoffs are evident in specific workloads; while LLM text generation for medium and large models ranks in the top 25%, text generation for small models falls into the bottom 10% at 33.18 tokens/sec. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage. Given the high memory bandwidth, 100 Gbps network baseline, and top-tier database operations and static web serving throughput, this server is suited for database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing.
